name: Iterative Re- on a Verb

1.definition: Forms a verb describing another performance of the relevant action.

projection.target: The normal reading presupposes an earlier check. A word that merely starts with the same letters, such as reject, need not support an again analysis.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Re- meaning do it again
curious.summary: Putting re- on the front of some verbs makes a new verb meaning to do the action again.
curious.body:
In Please recheck the numbers, recheck means to check them another time. The normal reading takes it for granted that there was an earlier check.

A word that only starts with the same letters, such as reject, doesn't necessarily mean again in the same way. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.
curious.try: Put re- on a verb like read or write. What does the new word mean, and what has to have happened first?

teacher.summary: Shows how re- builds verbs meaning to perform an action again.
teacher.explain: The prefix re- plus a suitable verbal base forms a verb describing another performance of the relevant action: Please recheck the numbers. The normal reading presupposes an earlier check. A word that merely starts with the same letters, such as reject, need not support an again analysis, so students shouldn't segment every re- word. This dictionary marks the account provisional and is built on one constructed example.
teacher.terms: Re- is traditionally a prefix; this dictionary calls the pattern iterative re- on a verb.
watch_for: A learner might split reject into re- plus ject and look for an again meaning.
A learner might use recheck when there was no earlier check.
teacher.activity: Students list re- verbs they know and sort them into again meanings and words where re- only appears at the start, then check each against a dictionary.

child.hook: What does the re- at the start of recheck do?
child.explain: Re- can mean again. To recheck is to check again. Something has to be checked first.
child.play: Add re- to verbs like read, write or play. Say what each new word means. Then use it in a sentence.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Iterative Re- on a Verb." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/re-iterative-prefix-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
